hook.line: A developer automated their entire job search, sent 700+ applications, and got hired.
hook.visual: A GitHub repo page (Career-Ops README) in a browser window on a macOS wallpaper; bold white uppercase captions build word by word, key word in yellow.

beats.what: Opens on the outcome while the browser window shows the repo README
Window starts moving as the caption builds 'entire job search'
Zoom punch: the window fills the frame on '700 applications'
Scroll up to the repo header with stars and the description: 'Career-Ops is the open source system'
Scroll down to the README's 'What is this' list while he names Stripe, Anthropic, OpenAI
Features table on screen for 'rewrites your CV with 14 skill modes'
Architecture diagram and dashboard section for 'ships with a terminal dashboard'
Zooms back out to the windowed view, matching the first frame for the loop

why_it_works: Outcome first ('got hired') before any explanation, so viewers stay to learn how
Concrete numbers (700 applications, 45+ companies, 14 modes) make the tool feel real
Scroll position follows the narration, so the README section on screen matches each claim
Ending zoomed out on the same window as frame one makes a near-seamless loop (0.953)
weaknesses: No face and a flat narrator voice; nothing personal in the account
README text is too small to read, so the screen is mood more than proof
No call to action and the line is cut off mid-sentence at the end
for_robert: Lead with the outcome in one sentence and a hard number, then show the proof; and end on the same framing as the first frame so the reel loops.
